labels.label: cor:K_lorentzien
labels.notes: Unmarked, partial. K_lorentzien assumes FirstCountable, T1, absolutely minimal, causally plain, and I^±(p) ≠ ∅ for all p. K_eq_I_of_pushUp has the push-up variant. minkowski_K_lorentzien is an instance and is disclosed as such. FINDING CHECKED, TRUE: the proof (l.889-891) never establishes causal plainness, which prop:tarentin_fort_K assumes (l.851). Two wording points for the author-facing text, not defects. First, 'tarentin and absolute minimality, which prop:tarentin_fort_K does not use' is true of its library proof: Kminus_eq_Iminus_of_mem_Zminus takes only FirstCountable, CausallyPlain and p ∈ Z^-, and this is already a ledger paper_finding on prop:tarentin_fort_K. The printed proposition does assume them, so say 'assumes but does not need'. Second, 'below Lipschitz regularity it fails' should read 'it can fail'.

It uses the reading K^-_U(A) = K^-_U(A ∩ U), which is the library's convention (le_mem_right) and is raised in questions. thesisRecursion_eq_empty (A ∩ U₁ = ∅ suffices) is strictly stronger. docstring_contract: All three files have a title, cite every label unmarked with the correct ETT.tex line (all 17 verified), and place the citations within the first 4000 characters. No ``**`label`**`` occurs anywhere. Each file has quoted blocks, a Hypothesis checklist, a SCOPE (disclosed) section and the Provenance line, and the SCOPE claims are true. Small defects are in minor finding 4: the BTZPoints checklist omits btz_past's IsCausal; two quotes silently drop a parenthetical reference; one quote has a bracket typo.

findings.what: The witness no_past_not_enough (radialLine) is tarentin at 0 only because it is non-local. Its relation -s ≤ t for |s| < |t| crosses the origin, and no curve in ℝ realises it. The natural local version of the same line (≤ generated by curves along which |·| increases) has J^-(t) = [0,t] for t > 0, and it is not tarentin at 0. So the REPORT's 'def:tarentin_spacetime reads only the relations of M itself, so non-locality does not matter for this point' is wrong. The witness is not a topological spacetime in the paper's sheaf sense, and kb/0019 asks such a refutation to be scoped to non-local causalities. Both findings that cite it are nevertheless TRUE for local causalities. Take ℝ² with x ≤_U y iff x = y or some curve in U along which |·| strictly increases joins them, and the same for ≪_U. This causality is causally arc-connected, hence absolutely minimal. It is causal and tarentin: at 0 take p = 0 and |q| = ε/2, so that J(0,q) contains the open disc of radius ε/2; at x ≠ 0 take p = (1-t)x and q = (1+t)x. And J^-(0) = {0}, J^+(0) = ℝ².
findings.fix: Delete the sentence 'non-locality does not matter'. Either scope the Lean evidence to non-local causalities (kb/0019) and add the planar argument as the reason the finding holds for the paper's causalities, or build the planar witness.

findings.what: 'the charts into E_α are not smoothly compatible with the regular charts; the cited smooth structure needs a smoothing along the singular lines' is unsupported and probably false. Give E_α ≅ ℝ³ the smooth structure of the coordinates (t, r cos(2πθ/α), r sin(2πθ/α)). The regular charts (local isometries into E^{1,2}, defined where r > 0) are then smooth in these coordinates, so they are compatible on every overlap, and the singular line is a smooth 1-submanifold. Brunswic2021cauchy Cor. 1.7 was not read. The sentence sits in a findings array and could be curated into the ledger as a statement about the cited construction.
findings.fix: Drop the sentence. 'The library has no smooth structure on a singular (G,X)-manifold, and no submanifolds' is a sufficient reason for not-attempted.
